comments.body:
## Phase 1 RCA — root cause PROVEN

**Root cause (changeable artifact):** `tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py:163-166`. The
test hand-rolls its request as `types.SimpleNamespace(app=..., query_params={...})` — an
INVALID stand-in for a Starlette `Request`, modelling only the query-param half of the auth
surface. Commit `4e8c83c833` ("66af: stop logging webhook/rerun token", 2026-08-04) widened
`_request_token` (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101`) to read `request.headers` FIRST and did
not update this fixture (`git show --stat 4e8c83c833` touches app.py, config.py and
tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_redaction.py — NOT this file). The attribute read raises
before any assertion runs.

## The central question, ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE: a header-less request is a TEST ARTIFACT, not a real production shape

Three discriminating experiments, all run in-venv (starlette 1.3.1 / fastapi 0.141.1 / py3.12):

**E1 — a real `Request` can NEVER raise `AttributeError` for `.headers`.**
`starlette/requests.py:132-136` defines `headers` as an unconditional `@property`; the scope
lookup happens inside `Headers(scope=...)` (`datastructures.py:519-522`, a bare subscript).
Observed:
- full scope -> `hasattr(r,'headers') is True`, type `Headers`
- scope with `headers` key DELETED -> raises **`KeyError('headers')`**, NOT AttributeError

This is the decisive discriminator: the observed `AttributeError` is only producible by an
object that is not a `Request` at all. No malformed ASGI scope can produce it.

**E2 — a real request with NO caller headers still has `.headers`.** Driving a FastAPI route
annotated `request: Request` via `TestClient` with zero caller headers yields
`{'type':'Request','mro':['Request','HTTPConnection','Mapping'],'has_headers':True,'headers_type':'Headers'}`.
"Header-less" at the HTTP level means an EMPTY `Headers` object, never a missing attribute.

**E3 — the production path is sound end-to-end.** `/rerun` driven through `TestClient` with
`GerritClient.get_change_event` raising `GerritError("SEKRIT ... stacktrace")`:
- legacy query-param auth, no `X-Rebar-Token` header at all -> `502 b'{"status":"gerrit error"}'`, leak-check True
- header auth -> `502 b'{"status":"gerrit error"}'`

Supporting contract citations: the ASGI HTTP connection-scope spec lists `headers` with no
"Optional" qualifier (unlike `scheme`/`raw_path`/`client`/`server`, which carry one); FastAPI
binds the `Request` param behind an `isinstance` gate
(`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:711`), whose only alternative is `WebSocket` — also an
`HTTPConnection`, also with `.headers`; and the repo already reads headers unguarded in the
same shape at `src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py:135`, with no `getattr(request,"headers",...)`
anywhere in `src/rebar/`.

**Therefore `_request_token` must NOT be made defensive.** A `getattr(request,"headers",None)`
would catch no real input, and if the impossible condition ever did occur it would SILENTLY
downgrade to the legacy `?token=` query branch — exactly the log-leaking path ticket 66af
existed to retire. The fix belongs in the test double.

`defect_legitimacy`: **defect** (in the test). Authoritative source: the ASGI scope spec plus
`starlette/requests.py:132-136` define what a `Request` is; a double omitting a mandatory
contract member is invalid. The repo's own convention agrees — every other review-bot handler
test (`tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_redaction.py:93-155`) drives handlers through
`fastapi.testclient.TestClient`; this hand-rolled fake is the lone outlier.

**Caller-dependency gate: CLEAR.** The change is confined to one test file; nothing depends on
the fixture.

## Correction to the report: this is NOT redding the CI Verified gate

The ticket states it reds CI. It does not — it is invisible there. The test is guarded by
`pytest.importorskip("fastapi")` (line 148) and **no CI lane ever installs fastapi**: all three
install steps in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` (lines 70, 219, 295) run
`uv sync --locked --extra dev`, and the `dev` extra contains no fastapi; `reviewbot` is also
absent from the `specs=(...)` isolation list in `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:169` (which
runs an import probe only, never pytest). Verified empirically: with `--extra dev --extra agents`
the test reports `SKIPPED [1] ... could not import 'fastapi'`. That CI blind spot is how
`4e8c83c833` earned `Verified +1` while breaking this test — it is a genuine second finding and
will be filed as a separate `discovered_from` ticket rather than fixed in this bug's scope.

## Report

`tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py::test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail` FAILS on current `origin/main` (reproduced standalone at 43ecfa8f27, and independently at 9bdb22f5887 before that):

```
AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'headers'
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101: in _request_token
    header_token = request.headers.get(TOKEN_HEADER, "").strip()
```

## Mechanism (unconfirmed — for the investigation to prove)

`_request_token` (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101`) reads `request.headers` unconditionally. The header path was added for ticket 66af (accept the token via header, keeping the query param for legacy Gerrit webhooks whose `webhooks.config` has not been re-pushed). The test constructs its request as a `types.SimpleNamespace` that predates that change and carries no `headers` attribute, so the attribute read raises before any assertion runs.

Whether the correct fix is to make `_request_token` tolerate a header-less request object, or to update the test's fake to match the real request contract, is EXACTLY the question the investigation must answer — a header-less request may be a real shape in production (some ASGI/test clients) or may be purely a test artifact. Do not assume.

## Why it matters

This is red on main. It reds the `Verified` CI gate for anyone whose change touches this suite, and it is a SECURITY-adjacent guard: the test exists to prove a 502 body carries no exception detail (path-injection guard). A guard test that errors before asserting proves nothing — the guarantee it is supposed to pin is currently unverified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The root cause is proven, with a cited mechanism, not guessed
- [ ] It is established and stated whether a header-less request is a REAL production shape or a test-only artifact, with evidence
- [ ] The test passes on a clean tree and actually exercises its original assertion (a 502 body containing no exception detail), not merely stops erroring
- [ ] A regression test fails against the pre-fix code and passes after
- [ ] The fix lands on main through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1
